treatment_suggestions.title: Rapid Transport for STEMI
treatment_suggestions.rationale: Patient has ST elevation on EKG (V1-V6), indicating acute myocardial infarction. Immediate transport to a facility capable of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is critical to minimize heart damage and improve outcomes.

treatment_suggestions.title: Rapid Transport for Stroke
treatment_suggestions.rationale: Patient has sudden onset of right-sided weakness and slurred speech, consistent with stroke. The patient is on NOAC (anticoagulant), which increases bleeding risk if thrombolytic therapy is needed. Rapid transport to a stroke center within the time window for reperfusion therapy is critical.

treatment_suggestions.title: Management of Febrile Seizure
treatment_suggestions.rationale: Patient had generalized seizure with fever. Immediate management includes ensuring patient safety, administering antipyretics (paracetamol), and transporting to a facility for further evaluation. The patient was given 250 mg oral dissolving paracetamol, which is appropriate for fever management.

treatment_suggestions.title: Management of Suspected Sepsis
treatment_suggestions.rationale: Patient has fever, chills, and cloudy urine, suggesting possible urinary tract infection progressing to sepsis. The patient was given paracetamol for fever and IV fluid for hydration. Rapid transport to hospital for antibiotics and further evaluation is critical to prevent progression to severe sepsis or septic shock.

drafted_journal: Journal 1: 62-year-old male with hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with sudden onset of central chest pain (4/10, pressing) radiating to left arm, beginning while resting. EKG shows ST elevations in V1-V6. Nitroglycerin (1 puff) provided no relief. Given ondansetron for nausea and 2.5 mg morphine for pain. Blood glucose 4.5 mmol/L, temperature 37.1°C. Prehospital diagnosis: STEMI. Recommendation: Transport to SÖS (Södersjukhuset) for acute angiography, priority 1. Under transport: Morfin and ondansetron effective, continuous EKG monitoring, defibrillator pads applied. Patient transported in cardiac position with continuous monitoring.
